news.title: How to watch New Zealand play for place at FIFA U-20 Men’s World Cup
news.lede: New Zealand play New Caledonia on Friday to decide which of the sides will qualify for next year’s FIFA U-20 Men’s World Cup. They meet in the semi-finals of the OFC U-19 Men’s Championship in Samoa, after Solomon Islands and Tahiti contest the other semi-final. The finalists at the OFC tournament will represent Oceania at next year’s FIFA U-20 Men’s World Cup in Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan. Both games will be streamed live and free by OFC Media via their YouTube channel.

news.title: French FA accuses Infantino of ‘seriously damaging’ football as it withdraws support
news.lede: ‘Image and unity’ of game affected, FFF president says. It will consult sacked former Fifa official Kevin Lamour. The French Football Federation’s president, Philippe Diallo, said Gianni Infantino had “seriously damaged the image and the unity of football” as he announced the end of France’s support for the Fifa president’s re-election. The FFF’s executive committee unanimously voted on Thursday to withdraw its backing, which had been formalised at the end of June.

news.title: Morocco claim they WILL host World Cup 2030 final reigniting blazing feud with Spain after Infantino claim
news.lede: THE head of the Moroccan FA claims the 2030 World Cup Final HAS been awarded to the North African country – to spark a renewed spat with co-hosts Spain. In the latest apparent sign that Fifa chief Gianni Infantino is using the location of the Final venue as a prong in his attempt to stave off attempts to oust him, Fouzi Lekjaa said the game “will” be played at the Grand Hassan II Stadium in Casablanca. The planned 115,000 capacity venue is not due to be completed until next year, while Spain has proposed Real Madrid’s Bernabeu or the Nou Camp in Barcelona. Fifa have declined to confirm the schedule or approved host cities for the next World Cup, although more than half the currently-agreed 104 matches will be played in Spain.

news.title: Saudi Arabia national football team: the full squad and key players, and why 25 of the 26 play at home
news.lede: Georgios Donis took 26 players to the 2026 World Cup and 25 of them play their club football in Saudi Arabia. Here is the full squad, the eight clubs it is drawn from, and what the Green Falcons take into the Gulf Cup they host in Jeddah from 23 September. Georgios Donis named 26 players for the 2026 World Cup, and 25 of them earn their living inside Saudi Arabia. That is not a quirk of one squad list.

news.title: FIFA delivers a fresh blow to Morocco: denies promising the 2030 World Cup final to the Hassan II Stadium
news.lede: Did Lekjaa rush the announcement of the World Cup final? FIFA have flatly denied ever promising Morocco the right to host the 2030 World Cup final. World football's governing body moved to shut down the row sparked by Fouzi Lekjaa, casting fresh doubt over the way the World Cup file is being wielded as a bargaining chip in FIFA's own power struggle. The denial followed some striking claims from a senior Moroccan football official, who insisted the tournament's showpiece in four years' time would be played at the Grand Stade Hassan II in Casablanca, a stadium still under construction.

news.title: Brazil: Carlo Ancelotti reveals his first squad list post-World Cup
news.lede: Eliminated in the Round of 16 of the World Cup by Norway, Brazil begins a new chapter under the guidance of Carlo Ancelotti. The Italian coach has unveiled a first squad that is significantly younger, featuring several new faces alongside some experienced players to assist in this transition. Carlo Ancelotti wants to quickly turn the page. Following a disappointing World Cup concluded with a defeat against Erling Haaland’s Norway in the Round of 16 (2-1), the Italian manager is now preparing for the future of the Seleção.

news.title: Did Lekjaa rush to announce the World Cup final? FIFA repeats its slap to Morocco
news.lede: "So far": the Hassan II Stadium will not host the finalFIFA have flatly denied any agreement or promise to hand Morocco the 2030 World Cup final. The decisive response ends the controversy sparked by Fouzi Lekjaa, and it deepens the doubts over whether the World Cup file is being used as a bargaining chip in the power struggle raging inside football's governing body.Their denial followed striking claims from a senior Moroccan football official, who insisted the tournament's showpiece, four years from now, would be staged at the Grand Stade Hassan II in Casablanca. That stadium is still under construction.An electoral statement that unsettles FIFASpanish newspaper " Marca " revealed the reply, citing an official FIFA spokesperson, and it was short and decisive: "As announced on 5 August 2026, FIFA will take a decision in due course."
